simple_explanation: Paracetamol is a fever reducer and pain reliever. It works in the brain to block chemical messengers (prostaglandins) that signal pain and regulate body temperature.
how_to_take: Take after food with water. Do not exceed 4000mg (6 tablets) in 24 hours. Maintain at least 4-6 hours between doses.
precautions: Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine to prevent liver toxicity.
Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing cold or flu remedies.
Consult a doctor if fever persists for more than 3 days.

simple_explanation: Calpol contains paracetamol to relieve pain and reduce high temperature safely.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours as required. Best taken after meals.
precautions: Avoid excessive consumption; overdosing causes severe liver strain.

simple_explanation: Pantoprazole reduces stomach acid production, healing heartburn and ulcers. Domperidone speeds up stomach emptying and prevents food from backing up into the food pipe, stopping nausea and regurgitation.
how_to_take: Take 1 capsule once daily in the morning, exactly 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast on an empty stomach with a full glass of water.
precautions: Do not crush or chew the sustained-release capsule.
Inform doctor if you have cardiac arrhythmias or kidney disease.
Long-term use may reduce Vitamin B12 and magnesium absorption.

simple_explanation: Reduces stomach acid and promotes normal stomach mobility to treat acid reflux and indigestion.
how_to_take: Take once a day in the morning before breakfast on an empty stomach.
precautions: Avoid spicy and greasy foods. Swallow whole.

simple_explanation: Amoxicillin is an antibiotic that kills bacteria. Clavulanic acid blocks bacterial enzymes (beta-lactamases) that would otherwise destroy amoxicillin, making the antibiotic effective against resistant bacteria.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet twice daily (every 12 hours) with or immediately after food to minimize stomach upset.
precautions: Always complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms resolve to prevent antibiotic resistance.
Do not take if you have a known penicillin allergy.
Stay well-hydrated.

simple_explanation: Azithromycin stops bacterial protein production, stopping bacteria from growing and allowing the immune system to clear the infection.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet daily at the same time, either 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.
precautions: Complete the 3 or 5 day regimen as prescribed.
Do not take antacids containing aluminum or magnesium at the same time.

typical_indications: Prevention of heart attacks and stroke
simple_explanation: Telmisartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of angiotensin II, a hormone that narrows blood vessels. This lowers blood pressure and eases the workload on the heart.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet daily with or without food, preferably at the same time each morning.
precautions: Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Do not take during pregnancy as it can harm the fetus.
Do not stop abruptly without doctor consultation.

typical_indications: Moderate to severe hypertension uncontrolled on monotherapy
simple_explanation: Dual mechanism: Telmisartan prevents blood vessel constriction, while Amlodipine directly relaxes blood vessel walls to effectively control persistent high blood pressure.
how_to_take: Take once daily in the morning.
precautions: May cause ankle swelling or mild dizziness when standing up quickly.

simple_explanation: Metformin decreases glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity. Glimepiride stimulates the pancreas to release more natural insulin. Together they maintain healthy blood sugar levels.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet once daily with the first main meal of the day (usually breakfast).
precautions: Carry glucose candy/lozenges in case of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
Avoid excess alcohol as it increases lactic acidosis risk.
Get HbA1c and renal function tests checked periodically.

simple_explanation: Sitagliptin enhances incretin hormones to prompt insulin release when blood sugar is high. Metformin curbs liver sugar production.
how_to_take: Take twice daily with meals to reduce stomach discomfort.
precautions: Inform doctor if experiencing severe persistent abdominal pain.

simple_explanation: Atorvastatin slows down liver production of LDL ('bad') cholesterol and triglycerides while raising HDL ('good') cholesterol, preventing arterial plaque buildup.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet once daily at bedtime, as cholesterol synthesis peaks during the night.
precautions: Avoid consuming large quantities of grapefruit juice.
Report unexplained muscle pain or tenderness immediately to your physician.

simple_explanation: Levocetirizine blocks histamine to eliminate sneezing and watery eyes. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes to decrease airway swelling and mucous production.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet daily in the evening or before sleep.
precautions: May cause mild drowsiness; avoid driving until you know how it affects you.
Not intended to treat acute sudden asthma attacks.

simple_explanation: Fexofenadine is a non-drowsy antihistamine that stops allergy symptoms like itchy throat, runny nose, and hives by blocking allergic histamine triggers.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet once daily with water. Avoid taking with fruit juices (apple, orange, grapefruit) as they decrease absorption.
precautions: Safe for daytime use since it rarely causes sedation.

simple_explanation: Combines ibuprofen (anti-inflammatory swelling reducer) and paracetamol (pain and fever controller) for comprehensive relief.
how_to_take: Always take after a full meal to protect stomach lining.
precautions: Avoid in patients with active peptic ulcer disease or kidney impairment.

simple_explanation: Cefixime inhibits bacterial cell wall formation, destroying susceptible bacterial pathogens.
how_to_take: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours for the duration prescribed by physician.
precautions: Do not skip doses. Complete entire prescribed course.
